answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making each identity expensive to earn, not just to create. Like a wharf that charges every ship a berth fee and logs its cargo, the network requires each agent to lock a small copper-value stake and complete verified tasks before it can transact at full limits. A bridge between new agents and trusted work then opens only after that record exists. An attacker wanting a thousand fakes must pay a thousand stakes and do a thousand jobs, so cloning identities stops paying.
